prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of commitments (ideological framing and names removed)

Brexit and trade
- Pass the existing withdrawal agreement, leave the EU in January 2020, negotiate an EU free trade agreement without extending the implementation period beyond December 2020; outside the single market, customs union and ECJ.
- Aim for 80% of UK trade under free trade agreements within three years (USA, Australia, New Zealand, Japan), strengthen Commonwealth ties, promote services trade, create up to 10 freeports.
- Maintain high environmental, animal welfare and food standards; NHS not part of trade talks.

Economy, tax and spending
- No rises in rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise NI threshold to £9,500 next year, with a longer-term ambition to raise tax-free earnings to £12,500.
- Fiscal rules: day-to-day spending not debt-funded; public investment to average ≤3% of GDP; reassess if debt interest reaches 6% of revenue.
- Invest ~£100bn in infrastructure; review and cut business rates, increase Employment Allowance, tackle late payments; anti-avoidance/evasion law and Digital Services Tax.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades; NHS visa.
- Mental and physical health treated equally; Innovative Medicines Fund; improve prevention, screening and hospital food; annual health tech summit; targeted free hospital parking.
- Social care: at least £1bn extra per year; cross‑party reform so no one has to sell their home to pay for care; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.

Education and skills
- Additional £14bn for schools; minimum per‑pupil funding; raise new teacher starting salaries to £30,000; back discipline, Ofsted, arts “premium,” PE, and SEND support.
- 20 Institutes of Technology; £3bn National Skills Fund; ~£2bn FE college upgrade; apprentices required on major projects; review student finance to reduce loan burden.

Policing, justice and immigration
- Recruit 20,000 police; tasers/body cams; Police Covenant; tougher sentencing for serious crimes; knife crime orders; 10,000 more prison places; parole reform; Royal Commission on criminal justice.
- New national cyber crime force and National Crime Laboratory; Online Harms legislation; Gambling Act review (including loot boxes, credit cards).
- Australian‑style points‑based immigration; fast‑track routes for NHS staff and top scientists; equal EU/non‑EU treatment; NHS surcharge increase; 5‑year residency for most benefits.

Housing, communities, transport and digital
- Build at least 1m more homes by mid‑2020s; 300,000/year target; “infrastructure first”; design codes; leasehold reform; shared ownership simplification; end “no‑fault” evictions; lifetime rental deposit; rough sleeping ended by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge for non‑residents.
- Towns Fund for 100 towns; youth services £500m; Safer Streets Fund; Community Ownership Fund £150m; support local media.
- Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester) and Midlands Rail Hub; restore Beeching lines; £1bn rapid EV charging (within 30 miles nationwide); consult on earliest phase‑out of new petrol/diesel cars; bus and cycling investments; gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas.

Business, innovation and science
- Increase R&D tax credit to 13% and include cloud/data; high‑risk research agency; unlock pension capital for innovation; use procurement to back new firms; review Entrepreneur’s Relief; support self‑employed.

Environment, farming and fisheries
- Net Zero by 2050; 40GW offshore wind by 2030; carbon capture cluster by mid‑2020s (£800m); £500m to decarbonise energy‑intensive industry; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; moratorium on fracking; new air quality laws.
- Environment Bill; Office for Environmental Protection; £640m Nature for Climate Fund (trees and peatland); plastics measures and deposit return; higher fly‑tipping penalties.
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; maintain farm budgets this Parliament; expand seasonal workers; leave CFP, legal duty to fish sustainably; coastal regeneration.

Union, democracy, defence and aid
- UK Shared Prosperity Fund to match and replace EU funds; devolution white paper; protect internal market access; restore NI institutions.
- Repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; update boundaries; voter ID; overseas voting rights restored; First Past the Post retained; commission on constitution, democracy and rights; update human rights/administrative law.
- Defence spending ≥2% of GDP and rising; modernise forces; Space Command; maintain nuclear deterrent; support veterans (legal protections, childcare, railcard, hiring incentives).
- Maintain 0.7% GNI for development; Magnitsky‑style sanctions; girls’ education; media freedom; anti‑slavery; health initiatives (maternal, newborn, child deaths; Ebola; malaria).

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; ban long transport for slaughter/fattening; extend ivory ban; restrict trophy imports; ban primates as pets; strengthen cat protections (including microchipping).
